thread.title: The stock market is in search for leadership following October's correction

author: Scott Gamm
title: The stock market is in search for leadership following October's correction
text:
The stocks that sparked October’s correction are the ones analysts think will lift the market higher.
Technology stocks, not financials, are set to continue their leadership streak once the market finds a bottom. That’s the assessment from multiple analysts who spoke to Yahoo Finance.
While Shawn Cruz, TD Ameritrade’s manager of trading strategy, acknowledged how strength in the financials sector is a bullish sign for the broader market, but he doesn’t think financials can go it alone, given how leveraged banks are to the economy.
“There needs to be participation from other cyclical sectors, such as industrials, technology and energy, not just because of their economic activity, but because these sectors make up such a large part of the market,” Cruz said. “Financials aren’t big enough to lift and keep the market higher on their own.”
Financials stocks represent roughly 13% of the S&P 500’s market capitalization. The information technology sector, which includes trillion-dollar Apple (AAPL) , makes up 21% of the index. And communication services, a new sector that includes tech giant Alphabet (GOOGL) , accounts for 10% of the S&P 500.
Apple CEO Tim Cook speaks during an event to announce new products Tuesday Oct. 30, 2018, in the Brooklyn borough of New York. (AP Photo/Bebeto Matthews) More Brian Levitt, a senior investment strategist with OppenheimerFunds, also expects the market to be led by growth areas, such as technology.
That’s in part because of another headwind facing financials: an aggressive Federal Reserve .
Even though banks tend to benefit from higher interest rates, which thicken their net interest margins, the strong dollar could keep the yield curve, a gauge of where interest rates stand, from steepening.
“I expect the U.S. [economy] to slow towards trend as the strong dollar and Fed tightening weigh on growth. That usually portends a flatter yield curve which doesn’t benefit financial stocks,” Levitt said.
A strong dollar is a byproduct of Fed rate hikes.
“If the Fed raises rates and growth slows, then long rates converge towards short rates. Long rates will come down as real GDP expectations come down,” he noted.
The Fed raised rates three times in 2018 and telegraphed a fourth hike for December.
Ken Leon, an equity analyst with Center for Financial Research & Analysis , has a Market Weight rating on the financials sector, and his firm maintains an Over Weight rating on the technology sector. “Financials have not had leadership for last 12 months,” he said. “They certainly did after Trump’s election.”
The data back up Leon’s point. Even with broader market selloff in October, the S&P 500 financials sector is down 8.8% since the start of the year, compared to a 6% gain for the information technology sector.
